report_name: Capcom Data Breach Exposes Data of Over 11 Million Users

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Actors
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actors responsible for the October 2026 data breach of Capcom's CAPCOM ID service, resulting in the theft of personal information from over 11.7 million users and the modification of 196 accounts.
threat_actors.goals: Data theft and potential account takeover for financial gain or resale.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Information Repositories
attack_patterns.description: Unauthorized actors gained access to the database of Capcom's CAPCOM ID service and exfiltrated personal information of over 11.7 million users, including email addresses, IP addresses, and login metadata.

attack_patterns.name: Account Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: Attackers illicitly changed the passwords for 196 user accounts as part of the data breach.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The report warns that the stolen user data, particularly email addresses, will likely be used in targeted phishing campaigns against the 11.7 million affected users. The provided indicators are designed to detect this anticipated follow-on activity.

identities.name: Capcom
identities.description: Japanese video game company and owner of the CAPCOM ID service that was breached, affecting 11.7 million users.

identities.name: CAPCOM ID users
identities.description: The class of over 11.7 million registered users of the CAPCOM ID service whose personal information was compromised in the data breach.

indicators.name: Capcom Phishing Lookalike Domain Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Capcom Phishing Lookalike Domain DNS Query
id: 9c5b1a3d-4e8f-4b1a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to potential lookalike domains used in phishing campaigns targeting Capcom users following the October 2026 data breach.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/capcom-confirms-data-breach-affecting-117-million-accounts/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-23
tags:
  - attack.t1566
  - attack.initial_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'capcom-security.com'
      - 'capcom-support.net'
      - 'capcom.security-update.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network requests to domains impersonating Capcom for phishing purposes, as suggested in the breach report.

indicators.name: Capcom Post-Breach Phishing Email Subject
indicators.pattern:
title: Capcom Post-Breach Phishing Email Subject
id: 8b4a09c8-3d7e-4a09-b6c5-8d9f0a1b2c3d
status: experimental
description: Detects emails with subject lines commonly used in phishing campaigns targeting Capcom users after a data breach.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/capcom-confirms-data-breach-affecting-117-million-accounts/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-23
tags:
  - attack.t1566
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: email
  category: email
detection:
  selection:
    Subject|contains:
      - 'CAPCOM ID Security Alert'
      - 'Your Capcom Account Requires Verification'
      - 'Resident Evil Special Offer Following Breach'
      - 'Your CAPCOM ID has been suspended'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects phishing emails with subject lines designed to exploit the Capcom data breach, as suggested in the report's hunting hints.
